issue: Over-claim on a Develop idea. A weld-process change is credited £19.77-£39.55/pack (risk-adjusted £13.84-£27.68, ~£1.7-3.3M/yr) because the class-default 15-30% band was applied to an affected cost of £131.83 that is 93% the cell (£122.41). The study's own Conversion sheet prices the entire laser-welding step at £1.36/pack, and the non-cell parts touched total £9.42.
evidence: Conversion: 'Laser welding, 26 joints | 3 min | £22/hr | machine £1.10 | labour £0.26'. Parts: cell £122.41, busbars £5.26, contacting system £3.80, NTC £0.36. Ideas ID-150 Saving basis: 'class default band, no part-specific estimate made'. Deck slide 82: class-default bands are 'almost all on parts below half a per cent of the bill of materials'.
recommendation: Re-estimate on the weld step and busbar content only (order of £1-2/pack before any Al-busbar benefit, which belongs to ID-008); remove the cell from the affected cost; withdraw the current figure from the Director deck.

issue: Over-claim on a Develop idea. 'Removes one layer of margin' is credited £27.24-£54.49/pack (risk-adjusted £19.07-£38.14). The study's own cascade carries only £8.21 SG&A + £8.71 profit on bought-in content and conversion plus a £1.84 cell handling charge (£18.76 total), and states the cell content already carries no pack-supplier SG&A or profit. The claimed saving exceeds the entire modelled margin layer.
evidence: Summary_Assembly: 'SG&A on bought-in and conversion 8.21 ... Cell content excluded from the base'; 'Profit on bought-in and conversion 8.71'; 'Cell handling charge 1.84'; 'EVE Energy manufactures both the cells and the pack. The cell price already carries a cell-maker's margin.' Saving basis: 'class default band'.
recommendation: Cap at the modelled margin actually removable (well under £18.76, net of in-house integration, warranty and safety-case cost the trade-offs list) and re-run the evaluation.

issue: Over-claim on a Develop idea: saving £4.11-£9.03 (risk-adjusted £2.87-£6.32) for deleting board-to-connector wiring, because the band is applied to the £40.00 user-stated BMS board. The signal connector is £1.05 and the whole internal sense harness £1.60; the board itself is not removed.

issue: Develop idea credits this pack's piece price with £2.32-£5.10 for freezing the interface for the NEXT programme; the tooling/fixture reuse it describes benefits future programmes, not this pack's should-cost.
evidence: ID-144 Cost mechanism: 'Tooling, fixtures, gauges and the leak test programme are all reused rather than rebuilt'; Specifics: 'carry-over interface for future 48V packs'. Tooling amortisation on this pack is only £0.92 (Summary_Assembly).

issue: Saving assumes the cell is energy-sized, but the study states the cell is sized for power (2.2x power-cell premium, A-01; ID-124 'the cell is bought at roughly 2.2 times an energy-cell price to survive 18 to 24C pulses'). A wider SOC window lowers power at the extremes (its own trade-off), and in 12S1P capacity can only fall by changing the cell Ah rating. Its validation text cites DO-02 to DO-04 while the trade-offs cite DO-02, DO-03 and DO-06.
evidence: ID-143 Trade-offs: 'reduces power at the extremes, which threatens DO-02, DO-03 and DO-06'; validationRequired: 'checking power capability at both ends against DO-02 to DO-04'. Assumptions A-01.
recommendation: Show that the cell is energy-limited before claiming £18-37/pack; reconcile the DO references.
